assessments.summary: The supplied proofs establish the numbered proper upper bound and the randomized, possibly improper lower bound under fixed uniform D. However, the declared claim additionally concludes, without qualification, that throughout 0<δ,ρ≤1/20 the restricted sample complexity is Θ(1/(ερ)). This is false when δ varies: accuracy itself requires Ω((1/ε)log(1/δ)) samples. The supported matching characterization is Θ(max{(1/ε)log(1/δ),1/(ερ)}) up to constants in the stated regime, or Θ(1/(ερ)) only with an added condition such as log(1/δ)=O(1/ρ), including fixed constant δ and ρ.
scopeQualifications: The half-interval geometry, version-space upper-bound analysis, and symmetric-coupling lower-bound proof are valid.
The upper bound is proper and fixed-uniform-distribution restricted.
The lower bound applies to randomized, computationally unbounded, possibly improper learners and proves n≥1/(120ερ) under the stated restrictions.
The worst-case corollary n_rep≥1/(120ερ) is valid for odd k in the stated regime because a worst-case learner must handle uniform D.
The restricted upper bound shows no log k factor for this fixed-uniform experiment, but does not upper-bound the class's unrestricted worst-case complexity under nonuniform distributions.
The coordinatewise tensorization discussion is explicitly heuristic and not a theorem for the original i.i.d. multidimensional construction.
evidenceIssues: The unqualified Θ(1/(ερ)) conclusion omits necessary confidence dependence. For two targets with disagreement p>2ε, the event that no sample hits their disagreement region has probability (1-p)^n; conditioned on it, at least one target fails with probability at least 1/2. Thus accuracy requires n≥log(1/(2δ))/(-log(1-p)).
In the stated regime one can choose p between 2ε and (5/2)ε, yielding n≥(3/(20ε))log(1/(2δ)). Hence arbitrarily small allowed δ decisively contradicts a uniform Θ(1/(ερ)) characterization.
No allowed dependency evidence was supplied or needed; the decisive defect and the valid subresults are established within the bounded report.
